A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoLDS Tensor-EM work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-system experiments and analyses of Area2 and PMd neural recordings in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds neural-data comparisons and diagnostic analyses, particularly in Appendix E.1.

M1.justification: The lagged-input reformulation, SMD tensor initialization, Ho-Kalman realization, residual-covariance initialization, and Kalman filter-smoother EM remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 retain the same procedures; additional explanations and evaluation configurations do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: The synthetic settings and Area2/PMd datasets are retained. v2 adds an Area2 multi-step and free-run forecasting scenario beyond one-step prediction (Figure 12), changing the observation-correction requirements. The 20-PC experiment changes configuration rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the neural comparisons: pure tensor joins both neural validation comparisons, independently fitted single-trial LDS joins the Area2 clustering comparison, and Random-EM joins the explicit clustering comparisons (Figures 5–6). v1 already included pure tensor on synthetic data, but not in these neural comparisons.

E3.justification: Added protocols include Area2 fitting with 20 PCs alongside six PCs, mild versus strong SLDS stickiness, and five-step/free-run prediction after a 100-ms warm-up. Existing model-selection metrics and hyperparameter grids are largely retained. Newly specified movement windows document existing experiments without establishing that their preprocessing changed.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 adds substantial checks of PCA information retention and dimensionality sensitivity, single-trial versus pooled/global LDS variability, SLDS stickiness, multi-step prediction failure, and non-dominant component responsibilities (Figures 7–9 and 11–13). These extend v1's narrower impulse-response and SLDS analyses.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports distributions of dominant and second-largest component responsibilities, making assignment uncertainty explicit (Figure 13), beyond v1's dominant-component maps and aggregate usage. This is a limited reporting addition; no additional run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are disclosed.

E6.justification: v2 adds pure-tensor neural scores, single-trial clustering comparisons, 20-PC results, and diagnostic findings including free-run drift and reported dominant/second responsibilities of 0.976/0.023. Neural validation NLL/BIC values also change between v1 Figures 4–5 and v2 Figures 5–6 without an explanation establishing a same-setting performance gain. The main synthetic recovery trends remain.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, moment construction, whitening, EM equations, covariance initialization, and complexity analysis are retained. The moment equation newly displayed in v2 Section 3.3 already appears in v1 Appendix A.2; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain SMD-based tensor initialization, noise-covariance initialization, and full EM refinement for reliable MoLDS recovery and interpretable neural clustering. Abstract compression and additional supporting experiments do not materially change these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains why pooled per-direction LDS fits are useful but imperfect references and interprets free-run divergence as compatible with identifying local dynamics. Section 6 also adds specific nonlinear/autonomous extensions and potential applications while retaining the existing model-mismatch limitation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies movement-onset windows of −100 to +500 ms for both neural datasets and documents the single-trial LDS comparison procedure. Dataset access and most implementation details remain unchanged. Both versions retain conflicting Area2 input descriptions: velocity in the main text versus six-dimensional force in the appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of decomposed and probabilistic decomposed LDS models, supporting neural-dynamics/application references, and more explicit attribution of the lagged-input and moment formulation to Rui and Dahleh. This expands context while retaining the central positioning relative to tensor methods and EM.

P1.justification: v2 edits and condenses the abstract, refines introductory and experimental prose, expands the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments and an LLM-usage statement. The principal section sequence and most methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The combined model/data overview is split and relocated, neural comparison panels are redesigned, the SLDS figure is expanded, and several diagnostic figures are added. The existing Area2 impulse-response panel moves from v1 Figure 4d to v2 Figure 10. These substantially restructure the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Additional pure-tensor and single-trial comparisons, PCA and stickiness checks, and explicit forecasting limitations better support and qualify the existing neural-clustering interpretation. The gain is useful but limited: several checks are qualitative or single-case, revised validation values are unexplained, and the conflicting Area2 input descriptions remain unresolved.
